component.name: Cabinet
component.summary: Windows VST plugins in per-plugin Wine prefixes

description.p: Cabinet packages Wine as a Flatpak so Windows VST2, VST3 and CLAP plugins can run on an immutable Linux system, giving every plugin its own Wine prefix — its own C: drive, registry and dependencies — instead of one shared prefix that every installer fights over.
Bridging is done by upstream yabridge. Only Wine runs inside the sandbox: the halves the DAW loads are exported to the host, so plugins appear in a native or Flatpak DAW as ordinary Linux plugins.

screenshot.caption: Every plugin in a Wine prefix of its own

description.p: Find a plugin in the Library, and close a manager you opened

ul.li: The Library has a search box and filters for category, developer, kind and whether it is installed, so a growing catalogue stays something you can look through
The managers you have installed sit in their own section at the top of the Library, each with a button that opens it and turns into one that closes it
A manager can be closed from its own page as well, and from the command line with cabinet library stop
The same narrowing works on the command line, as --search, --category, --developer, --kind and --installed

description.p: Demos install themselves, and a closed DAW leaves nothing behind

ul.li: A plugin that offers a demo can download it instead of asking for an installer you bought — Melodyne is the first, and either route lands in the same prefix with the same Wine settings
Plugins appear as an installer writes them: the prefix is watched while a Library app runs, so what an installer leaves on its way out is picked up
Closing a DAW now closes the Wine sandbox it started, instead of leaving bridge processes running behind it
An error from the X server no longer takes Wine down with it, so a plugin's window closing at the wrong moment does not end the plugin
Doctor's memlock advice names both systemd configuration files and says to reboot

description.p: Klevgrand's whole catalogue joins the Library

ul.li: The Klevgrand Helper installs and authorises every Klevgrand product an account owns, and every one of them as a fully functional demo
A Library entry can ship a payload archive of its own alongside its script, which is how the Helper gets the archive tool its prefix lacks
Opening an app waits for the prefix's own Wine processes to finish, so plugins an installer writes on its way out are seen instead of missed

description.p: Melodyne joins the Library

ul.li: Melodyne 5 studio's 30-day trial can be downloaded, installed silently and bridged as a VST3 plugin

description.p: A virtual desktop for editors that need one, and prefixes that say when they have drifted

ul.li: `cabinet set <name> desktop <WxH>` runs a prefix's windows inside one Wine desktop of that size, keeping a bridged editor's clicks landing where you point them; the prefix page carries the same switch
Doctor warns when a prefix's sync mode has drifted from what an installed plugin's entry asks for
Wine launched through the shim can no longer end up on Wayland either, closing the same door already closed for a prefix launched directly
Serum 2 turns off two of its own preferences that fought its Direct2D runner's drawing
Plugin descriptions no longer explain how Cabinet installs a plugin, only what it is and what it costs to run

description.p: Eighteen more plugins, and Windows plugins that come back out again

ul.li: Auburn Sounds' eight free editions — Graillon 3, Couture, Panagement 2, Lens, Renegate, Inner Pitch 2, Psypan 2 and Selene — as Linux builds, so none of them needs Wine
Valhalla's three free plugins — Supermassive, Freq Echo and Space Modulator — sharing one prefix between them
Madrona Labs' five — Aalto, Aaltoverb, Kaivo, Sumu and Virta — sharing one prefix, each installing with no wizard to click through
Sitala, both the free version 1 and the current one
Removing a Windows plugin runs the plugin's own uninstaller and leaves everything else in the prefix standing, instead of asking you to delete the prefix and start again
Doctor says when a prefix points at a runner that is no longer installed, and when a plugin sits in a prefix that has drifted off the Wine its editor needs

description.p: Eight more plugins, and prefixes that stop writing into your home

ul.li: All six of TAL's free plugins — NoiseMaker, Filter-2, Reverb-4, Chorus-LX, Vocoder and Bitcrusher — as Linux builds, so none of them needs Wine
FabFilter's Total Bundle: all fourteen of their plugins from one installer, on a 30-day trial
Vital, whose download sits behind an account — Cabinet opens the login page and installs the file you come back with

A prefix keeps its Documents, Desktop and Music inside itself instead of pointing them at yours, so a plugin that writes there installs everything it should: Serum 2 had been laying down its binary and none of the 1.4 GB of wavetables, presets and skins its editor needs
Serum 2 installs unattended now, with no wizard to click through
Where a vendor serves one always-current download there is nothing to check it against, and both the window and the command line say so before fetching

description.p: A prefix made before this release is repaired the next time a plugin is installed into it.
Small fixes to the logos
Plugins have pages, and installs that a tar cannot do

ul.li: Every plugin in the Library gets a page of its own: a screenshot, what it is, who makes it, which formats it installs as and what running it costs
Seven free u-he synths added — Podolski, Triple Cheese, Protoverb, Zebralette 3, TyrellN6, ZebraCM and BazilleCM
A catalogue entry can name an install script for the plugins a plain unpack cannot install, and say which directory of its own a plugin keeps presets in
cabinet library show tells you the same as the page does
Removing a Linux plugin now asks first, and says what it will delete
Downloads show how far along they are: a bar in the window, percentages on the command line

description.p: Removing a u-he plugin also deletes its presets, which live in ~/.u-he.
A Library page, so a plugin installs itself

ul.li: Pick a plugin and it is downloaded, checked, installed and bridged for you
Windows plugins ask whether to use a prefix you have or make a new one, then pin the Wine their editor needs and add DXVK without being told
Plugins you had to buy carry the same knowledge and ask for your installer
Linux plugins need no Wine at all: VST3, CLAP and LV2 land in Cabinet's own directory and are linked where your DAW looks, and remove takes them out cleanly
The enrol command can be copied out of the window now

description.p: Enrolled DAWs need `cabinet enrol` run again to see Linux plugins; bridged Windows plugins keep working untouched.
Taking DXVK out can no longer delete Wine's own Direct3D

ul.li: Turning the switch off on a prefix DXVK was never in is refused, not obeyed
A prefix Wine could not repair keeps saying so, rather than reading as clean
Asking for dxvk anything but on or off is refused, not taken as off

description.p: Prefixes carry their own settings

ul.li: A sync primitive per prefix: system, esync, fsync or ntsync
Environment variables per prefix, reaching bridged plugins too
DXVK is a switch now, and putting it back restores the DLLs it replaced
New prefix and Wine versions moved onto the pages they act on

description.p: Fixed the external link icons

An About page names the running build: its version, the remote it was installed from and whether that remote is the published repository or a local one, the bundled yabridge and Wine, and where Cabinet keeps its prefixes, runners and sockets. The same is printed by `cabinet about`.

The Wine versions list reads the component index Bottles reads instead of GitHub's API, which rations unauthenticated callers and made the list fail with a message about a host it had in fact reached. More builds are listed, a failure says what actually went wrong, and Soda's downloads now carry a checksum.
The Wine versions list is grouped into families the way Bottles groups its runners, and Soda joins Kron4ek as a second source. Versions are no longer labelled with a verdict of their own.
First release under Cabinet's own version. Wine 11 and yabridge 5.1.1, per-plugin prefixes on downloadable Wine runners, DXVK, enrolment for Flatpak DAWs, and a GTK4 window beside the command line.
